findings.title: SQL injection via f-string in search_orders_advanced
findings.explanation: search_orders_advanced builds SQL with f-string interpolation of query, allowing SQL injection. Existing search_orders uses parameterised LIKE; this new function regresses that protection.

evidence.why: f-string interpolates user query directly into SQL LIKE clause
SQL built with f-string embedding raw query instead of ? placeholder

findings.suggestion: Use parameterized query with ? placeholder for LIKE pattern, e.g. WHERE status LIKE ? with (f"%{query}%",).
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed f-string SQL with direct interpolation in new function; parameterized fix is concrete.

findings.title: Hardcoded AWS key in shop/uploads.py
findings.explanation: New module commits an AWS access key as a source-code constant. Any clone or leak exposes the credential and prevents rotation without code change. Load from environment or secrets manager instead.

evidence.why: hardcoded credential constant introduced by this diff in new file

findings.suggestion: Remove hardcoded key and load from environment or secrets manager.
findings.verifier_note: Real code location with concrete fix; kept per secret policy with moderated confidence without validating secret value.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-user order disclosure in orders_search2
findings.explanation: orders_search2 drops the User dependency used by orders_search/orders and calls search_orders_advanced which has no user_name filter, so any unauthenticated caller can enumerate all users' orders via /orders/search2.

evidence.why: endpoint takes only q with no User auth and calls unscoped all-users search
advanced query has no user_name filter unlike scoped search_orders

findings.suggestion: Require User auth on orders_search2 and scope query by user_name like orders_search/search_orders.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed new endpoint lacks User and calls unscoped query; cross-user exposure introduced by diff.
